ideas.description: I100 rebased onto the current tip. Base: E090 code (48b13a7): 2@16 + 1.25@24 at bs 1536, then 1.25@28 + 2.75@32 at bs 1024, with pinned staging and the Fable tail. Because the tip indexes by samples, the final-EMA window and the lookahead stop cover the same sample count as the bs-1536 tip, which is ~12 steps at bs 1024 (~3 EMA updates). Change only this: pin both to step counts measured from the end, so the final EMA covers the last 8 steps (lerp 0.3 every 4 steps, ~2 updates) and lookahead stops 8 steps before the end. The floor-hold point stays sample-indexed and unchanged. This is a host-side step-index change only and nothing recompiles. Precondition, untimed: log the source hash and a one-line diff against 48b13a7. Decide with an off-seed run on seeds 3-10 against the tip off-seed distinct mean (~0.7526, sd ~0.09 pp, E094), plus two scored runs. If it is accepted, use the pinned window in every later bs-1024-tail arm.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%, ~4.46 s). E081 showed a 20-step window costs ~0.09 pp against 8 steps, so interpolation puts the current ~12-step window at about -0.03 to -0.05 pp. Pinning should recover +0.03 to +0.10 pp: off-seed ~0.7530-0.7537 and a scored pool of ~0.7528-0.7540. It is banked as the tip if the off-seed delta is >= +0.03 pp and both scored runs are feasible. If the off-seed delta is <= 0, E084's +0.11 pp came from extra updates and not from the window, which supports H10 and leaves the window as it is.

ideas.description: Equal-time reallocation between two measured exchange rates. The 24 px bridge appears to buy ~0.13 pp per 1% (E064/E065 vs E070/E071, and the E070 trim cost ~0.14 pp per 1%). Substituting 28 px for 32 px costs only ~0.02 pp per 1% (E090: about -0.1 pp off-seed against E084 for -4.6% time). Base: E090 code. Change only the schedule to 2@16 + 1.5@24 (bs 1536) + 2@28 + 2@32 (bs 1024). Switches are indexed by samples. LR warmup/decay, the floor-hold, the final-EMA window, the lookahead stop and the renorm cadence are rescaled by samples exactly as E084/E090 do (samples rise by 0.25 epoch; steps rise by ~8). All shapes are already static and warmed up in build. Pre-registered time: +0.25 epoch at 24 px (~+0.125 s) and 0.75 epoch moved from 32 to 28 px (~-0.13 s), so equal time ±0.6%. Decide with an off-seed run on seeds 3-10 plus two scored runs.
ideas.expected: Time 4.43-4.49 s (equal to the tip within ±0.6%). Accuracy +0.0 to +0.12 pp against the tip: off-seed ~0.7528-0.7538 and a scored pool of ~0.7525-0.7540. The bridge should gain ~+0.08-0.15 pp and the extra 28 px should cost ~-0.04 to -0.07 pp. If it is accepted (off-seed >= tip +0.05 pp, both scored runs feasible), it becomes the tip, and later time cuts come from more 32->28 substitution. If the off-seed delta is <= -0.05 pp, either the 24 px bridge gain was mostly noise or the 28 px substitution rate is steeper beyond 1.25 epochs. A follow-up that changes only one of the two halves would tell them apart.

ideas.description: I101 rebased onto the current tip (its old base, E086, is superseded). Base: E090 code, which already has the samples-indexed _fit. Run the 16 and 24 px phases at bs 1024 instead of 1536, which adds ~53 steps. The 28/32 px phases and the whole tail stay as on the tip. LR warmup/decay, the floor-hold and the renorm cadence are indexed by samples. Scale the SGD groups per phase by the kilostep rule and leave Muon lr and momentum unchanged. Compile static bs-1024 16/24 px shapes, including the whitening-bias-grad variant at 16 px, and warm them up in build. Decide with an off-seed run on seeds 3-10 plus one scored run. Compare the gain per added step with E084 (+0.11 pp off-seed for ~65 tail steps).
ideas.expected: Time +1.5 to +2.5% (about 4.53-4.57 s), because the low-res phases are per-step-bound at ~2 ms per step. Placement-independent prediction: off-seed +0.05 to +0.15 pp. A gain of >= +0.2 pp means early updates are worth more than late ones. A follow-up would then fund the early bs 1024 with more 32->28 substitution, at a net-better rate than the tip. A gain of <= 0 means updates only matter late, which closes early-phase batch levers. Not a tip candidate on its own, because it is slower.

ideas.description: On the current tip (E090 code), change only the conv-filter Muon peak lr from 0.24 to 0.28 through its 0-d tensor. The head keeps its 0.5x multiplier, so its lr scales along, and nothing recompiles. The schedule shape, floor and tail are unchanged. Muon lr was only ever tuned at bs 1024 with ~384 steps on a pre-tail base (E034). The tip now has ~280 steps, mixed batch sizes and a floor-hold tail, so the optimum may have moved up. Decide with an off-seed run on seeds 3-10 against the tip's distinct mean, plus two scored runs.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Accuracy -0.15 to +0.15 pp. If the off-seed gain is >= +0.12 pp (about 1.3x the calibrated sd) and the scored pool is >= tip +0.05 pp, it is a free margin source and becomes the tip. If it is within ±0.1 pp, run 0.20 off-seed only once; if that is flat too, Muon lr is closed for good. A loss of >= 0.15 pp means 0.24 is at or above the optimum.

ideas.description: Explore the lookahead strength. E092 showed the SGD-era lookahead-EMA is worth ~0.2-0.3 pp under Muon (removing it cost -0.18 pp off-seed), but its strength was never tuned for Muon. Base: E090 code. Precondition, free: log the lookahead cadence and decay schedule in step terms for both batch-size phases. Change only the per-update decay base, so the effective averaging horizon is ~1.5x longer: for alpha_t = base^k * progress^p, set (1-base_new) = (1-base_old)/1.5. Cadence, the progress exponent, the stop point and the final EMA stay unchanged. This is a 0-d tensor or host-side constant and nothing recompiles. Decide with an off-seed run on seeds 3-10 plus two scored runs.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Accuracy -0.15 to +0.15 pp. Removing the lookahead was costly, so a mild extension may add +0.05 to +0.1 pp. If the off-seed gain is >= +0.1 pp and the scored pool is >= tip, it becomes the tip and the opposite direction is not run. If it is <= -0.1 pp, the current horizon is at or past the optimum, and lookahead tuning closes after one shorter-horizon probe.

ideas.description: Explore in the TSLA direction, which the H6.7 re-scoping favours over lower early LS. Base: E090 code. Use label smoothing 0.3 for the first 80% of samples and 0.1 for the last 20%, which falls inside the 32 px phase and covers the floor-hold. Pass LS as a 0-d tensor into the compiled loss so the 32 px graph is not duplicated. If that is not possible, compile and warm both 32 px variants in build. Smoke-test 10 steps for a finite loss. Change nothing else. Decide with an off-seed run on seeds 3-10 plus one scored run, and a second scored run only if off-seed >= tip +0.1 pp.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Low prior: uniform LS changes were null (E009, E037) and MaxSup lost 0.18 pp (E078). Expected -0.15 to +0.1 pp. Off-seed >= tip +0.12 pp would make phase-dependent LS a free margin source. A result within ±0.1 pp closes H6.7. A loss of >= 0.15 pp shows that LS's target-side term matters most at the end of training.

ideas.description: Mechanism test, run off-seed only. On the current tip code (E090), replace the final EMA with E083's LAWA (a uniform mean of 5 snapshots every 4 steps over the last 20 steps). Also average the BN running_mean/running_var buffers over the same snapshots with the same 1/k running-mean lerp, instead of copying them from the final net. Buffers are allocated in build and reset in prepare. Run seeds 3-10 off-seed in an untimed side script and compare with E083's -0.29 pp loss against the tip. For the scored row, rerun the unchanged tip E090 code once, which adds a distinct tip sample to the thin tip pool (currently ~0.7524 over two distinct runs).
ideas.expected: Scored row: a tip rerun at ~4.46 s and 0.751-0.754. Off-seed: under the BN-mismatch explanation, the loss against the tip shrinks to <= 0.1 pp. In that case, also averaging BN buffers in the current 8-step final EMA is a candidate free gain worth one A/B. If the loss stays >= 0.2 pp, averaging higher-LR pre-floor iterates is the cause, and end-of-run averaging closes for good.

drop.reason: Stale base: it runs on E084 code with staging, but E090 (28 px substitution on that base) is now the tip, and the same EMA-window confound applies there. Re-proposed as the pinned 8-step window on E090, where a positive result can be banked directly.

Stale base: it targets E086 code, but the tip is E090 (bs-1024 28/32 px tail). Re-proposed unchanged in substance on E090, so its off-seed delta is measured against the current tip's calibrated off-seed baseline.

structured_output.summary:
The tip, E090 (2@16 + 1.25@24 at bs 1536, then 1.25@28 + 2.75@32 at bs 1024; ~4.46 s), averages about 0.7524 over two distinct scored runs and about 0.7526 off-seed (sd ~0.09 pp, E094). That is below the 0.753 gate, so roughly half of reruns fail. Accuracy at equal time comes before any further cut.

The best measured exchange rate is substituting 28 px for 32 px, at about 0.02 pp per 1% of time. The 24 px bridge looks like the most valuable time in the run, at about 0.13 pp per 1%, though that estimate is noisy.

New queue, 7 ideas:
- **Pinned 8-step final-EMA window on E090 (priority 5, exploit).** The bs-1024 tail currently averages over ~12 steps, which removes the confound in I100.
- **Equal-time reshuffle 2@16 + 1.5@24 + 2@28 + 2@32 (priority 4, exploit).** It moves time from the 32 px phase into the 24 px bridge, combining the two measured rates.
- **H10 placement test rebased onto E090 (priority 2, explore).**
- **Filter Muon lr 0.28 (priority 2, exploit).**
- **Longer lookahead horizon (priority 2, explore).** Lookahead proved worth 0.2-0.3 pp under Muon but was never tuned for it.
- **TSLA-direction phase-dependent label smoothing (priority 1, low-prior explore).**
- **H6.5.4 BN-averaging diagnostic (priority 1).** It runs off-seed only, and its scored row is a tip rerun that adds a sample to the thin tip pool.

I100 and I101 are dropped because their bases are out of date; both are re-proposed on E090.
